source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Decide if you can accept or reject each item. If unsure, get advice.
3. Record your decision and reasons for this with the appropriate forms for essential and non-essential safety features.
4. If you rejected an item, decide what to do about the safety feature, decide what to do about the issue, document actions and the timeframes for corrections and get consent from the management.
6. Repeat the inspection in the appropriate timeframes.

## Introduction
Under the [Queensland Building Act 2021](https://www.legislation.qld.gov.au/view/pdf/inforce/current/act-2021-015) (Building Act), a building certifier needs to carry out prescribed fire safety inspections (PFSIs) for certain building classes. This includes annual checks and after an incident that could affect a building's fire safety.
